title: Sensible vs Latent Load & Environmental Capacity

content.overview: Controlled rooms carry both heat and moisture loads. Temperature can remain controlled while humidity rises, so specialists must distinguish sensible cooling performance from latent moisture-removal performance.

vocabulary.definition: Heat load that changes air temperature.
Moisture load associated with water vapor that must be removed or condensed.
Available control capacity beyond the current operating load.

sections.title: Stable temperature does not prove moisture control
sections.body: If RH rises sharply after irrigation while temperature stays stable, investigate latent moisture-removal capacity and sequencing before assuming a sensible-cooling problem.

sections.title: Crop load changes through the cycle
sections.body: Transpiration and environmental load shift with biomass, light, root-zone water and developmental stage. Empty-room or early-cycle performance does not prove late-cycle capacity.

sections.title: Temperature response is crop-context dependent
sections.body: Cannabis temperature studies show genotype-specific crop responses, so equipment performance and crop response should be evaluated without turning one experimental treatment into a universal setpoint.

workedExamples: A room holds temperature but loses RH control after irrigation events as canopy biomass increases; that pattern is consistent with a latent-load limitation worth qualified system review.
commonMistakes: Treating temperature and humidity as one load.
Changing room targets before confirming the actual load pattern.
content.practicalApplication: Plot temperature, RH, lighting state and irrigation events over several days and classify periods where sensible and latent control diverge.
content.summary: Environmental capacity has separate heat and moisture dimensions that must be diagnosed with trend evidence.
